> 魯有兀者王駘，從之遊者與仲尼相若。

In Lu there is a man whose foot has been amputated, and the number of students following him equals Confucius's.

## 兀 is an amputation, and it is placed first

兀: the punishment of cutting off the foot, 刖, also written 跀.

The chapter opens with three 兀者 in a row — men marked by the most visible form of social disgrace. That placement is the argument: whatever this chapter is about to call 德 has nothing to do with the mark.

## 符 is a tally that matches

符 in the pre-Qin was a credential split in two; when the halves meet, it verifies. 德充於內，外顯感應 — virtue fills inside, and the outside answers.

The distinction matters: 符 is a verification, not an application. It is not that you first manufacture the appearance of virtue in order to be recognized. It is that the inside is full, and then the outside lines up.

Which is why this is not a chapter about charisma. Charisma is the appearance produced in advance.

## 才全 is not talent

才: innate endowment, the vital capacity you were born with. 全: whole, unharmed, still in tune.

才全 is not "fully talented." It is: the inner vitality is intact and in tune, and no event outside has knocked it out of alignment.

## 滑和: the outside does not disturb the tuning

滑: to disturb, to muddle. 和: the inner harmony.

Poverty and success, misfortune and favor — none of them 滑和. The measure of a person is not what happened, but whether the happening got into the tuning.

## 兌 is 悅

通而不失於兌 — unobstructed without losing 兌. 兌 here reads 悅, delight.

Read this character dead and the whole passage becomes numbness: a person so equanimous that nothing reaches them. The text says the opposite: open all the way through, and still glad.

## 益生: adding to life is ill-omened

益生: to add to life artificially — extra likes and dislikes, extra cleverness, extra disciplines, extra names for self-improvement.

This word comes straight from 老子 chapter 55, 益生曰祥 — where 祥 is used in its ominous sense. 莊子 keeps the same verdict and moves it: 老子 speaks of the body's allotment, 莊子 of the wear on the mind.

The two books are not vaguely similar here. It is one sentence with two landings.

## The test

Name one quality you cultivate because it verifies well — a credential, a reputation for calm, a habit other people praise. Then ask the 符 question: is it full inside, or is it an appearance prepared in advance? A tally that matches can be checked. A badge cannot.
